What’s your possible?
At Northrop Grumman UK, you are part of a team driving innovation where it matters most, solving tomorrow’s challenges and shaping the technology solutions of the future. It’s what we call Defining Possible.
This mindset goes beyond our customer solutions; it is the foundation for your career development and the impact we have within the communities where we live and work.
This is more than just a job. It’s a mission.
We are looking for a Management Systems and Audit Manager to join our Quality & Mission Assurance team. In this influential leadership role, you will help shape and strengthen the governance, compliance and assurance framework that underpins our business operations.
You will be responsible for maintaining and developing our Integrated Management System (IMS), ensuring continued compliance with internationally recognised standards including ISO 9001, ISO 20000-1, ISO 27001 and ISO 14001. You will also play a key role in supporting the achievement of future certifications aligned to business strategy.
Alongside management systems leadership, you will oversee a risk-based audit programme, delivering meaningful assurance activities that drive continuous improvement, support operational excellence and contribute to Northrop Grumman UK's mission of delivering critical capabilities across defence, cyber, engineering and mission systems.
This is an exciting opportunity to lead a specialist team, influence stakeholders across the business and make a measurable impact on how we continually improve and grow.
What you'll be doing
As Management Systems and Audit Manager, you will:
• Lead the development, maintenance and continuous improvement of Northrop Grumman UK's Integrated Management System, ensuring compliance with industry and regulatory standards.
• Manage the organisation's external ISO certification portfolio and support the attainment of new certifications that enable strategic growth.
• Develop and oversee a three-year risk-based audit programme covering internal processes, programmes, suppliers, customers and external assurance activities.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives by partnering with process owners and business functions to enhance efficiency, effectiveness and compliance.
• Lead and develop the Management Systems and Audit team, providing coaching, support and professional development opportunities.
• Monitor performance metrics, identify trends, risks and opportunities, and provide meaningful reporting to senior stakeholders.
What we’re looking for
We're interested in hearing from people who can demonstrate:
Essential
• Proven experience managing and improving integrated management systems within a regulated environment.
• Strong knowledge of management system standards and regulatory compliance requirements.
• Experience creating, managing and delivering risk-based audit programmes.
• Lead Auditor qualification.
• Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and build strong working relationships across all levels of an organisation.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
Desirable
• Auditor qualification and/or working knowledge of one or more of the following standards: ISO 27001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, ISO 44001, ISO 31001 or ISO 22301.
• Experience working within defence, security, engineering, technology or other highly regulated sectors.
• Experience using SharePoint and digital management systems.
•
If you do not meet every requirement but have relevant skills, experience and the passion to succeed, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and recognise that talent comes from many different backgrounds.
Security Clearance
Due to the nature of our work, you must be eligible to obtain and maintain the appropriate UK Government security clearance for this role.
You must be able to gain and maintain the required UK Government security clearance as a condition of employment.
Our recruitment team is on hand to answer any questions and will guide you through the process: talentenquiries@uk.ngc.com
Benefits
We believe in supporting our people both professionally and personally. Our benefits include:
• Flexible working options, including compressed fortnight arrangements where applicable
• Private healthcare
• Cash health plan
• Holiday purchase and sell scheme
• Competitive pension scheme
• Career development and learning programmes
• Performance-based bonus opportunities
• Employee assistance programme
• Life assurance
• Wellbeing initiatives and support networks
Why Join Northrop Grumman UK?
A Mission to Believe In
Every day, we contribute to building a more secure and connected world. Our teams work on meaningful programmes that protect national interests, advance technology and help solve complex challenges.
A Place to Belong and Thrive
We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected and empowered to contribute. Every voice matters at our table, and collaboration is central to how we succeed.
Your Career, Your Way
Whether you are looking to deepen your expertise, expand your leadership capability or explore new career paths, Northrop Grumman UK provides opportunities, mentoring and development programmes to help you achieve your ambitions.
Ready to apply?
Yes – Submit your application online.
Possibly – Reach out to our team for more information at talentenquiries@uk.ngc.com
No – Explore our other opportunities. We’re growing across the UK and are always looking for talented people who want to help define what’s possible.
Northrop Grumman is committed to hiring and retaining a diverse workforce, and encourages individuals from all backgrounds and all abilities to apply and consider becoming a part of our diverse and inclusive workforce.

Job Description:
Salary: Senior: £45, 200 to £61,950 / Principal: £53,300 to £71,400
Leonardo UK operates a grade-based salary framework with broad bands. The salary range shown reflects the approved grade band for this role, or a narrower hiring range published within that band, and is benchmarked against the external market. Exceptions above the standard range are managed through governance controls to protect internal equity.
Your Impact
Join us at Leonardo and become part of a team shaping the next generation of radar technology. We’re looking for talented, driven, and experienced RF/Microwave Engineers to join our expanding hardware engineering community within our world‑class radar division, based at our Edinburgh site.
As an RF Engineer, you’ll play a pivotal role in developing and delivering cutting‑edge radio‑frequency systems that sit at the heart of our advanced defence solutions. Your expertise will help ensure these systems perform with precision, reliability, and excellence in some of the most demanding environments in the world.
What you’ll bring
To excel in this role, you’ll bring a strong command of RF circuit design, microwave engineering, and electromagnetic theory, paired with the problem‑solving mindset and attention to detail needed to tackle complex technical challenges. A curiosity for emerging technologies, enthusiasm for the defence and space sectors, and adaptability to new methods and tools will also help you thrive as part of our team. You will:
•
Lead a series of applied research work-packages and feasibility studies, document and report on their findings, and provide RF architectural recommendations to support the creation of a digital antenna concept for our next generation surveillance radar system
•
Create high quality and robust designs; fully document and record your work products, keep them under configuration management and provide plans and progress reports; and conduct design reviews within the design review framework
•
Supervise junior responsible engineers from within your system or functional block of RF assemblies
•
Ensure design reviews are planned, executed and completed successfully
•
Prepare robust manufacturing data packs and provide technical support to sub-contracts and engineering interface with manufacturing
•
Qualifications: first or second degree (BSc, BEng, MEng, MSc, PhD, EngD) in Electrical & Electronic Engineering (preferable) or related science (e.g. Physics)
•
Proven experience (5 years +) in RF circuit design and analysis and a strong understanding of microwave techniques and electromagnetic theory
•
Proficiency in using commercial software tools for RF analysis /simulation and schematic capture such as ADS, AWR, CST
Security Clearance
This role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV). For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting
Why join us
At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.
•
Time to Recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year.
•
Secure your Future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution.
•
Your Wellbeing Matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity).
•
Rewarding Performance: All employees at management level and below are eligible for our bonus scheme.
•
Never Stop Learning: Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn Learning.
•
Refer a friend: Receive a financial reward through our referral programme.
•
Tailored Perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.
•
Flexible working: Flexible hours with hybrid working options. For part time opportunities, please talk to us about what might be possible for this role.
For a full list of our company benefits please visit our website.
Leonardo is a global leader in Aerospace, Defence, and Security. Headquartered in Italy, we employ over 53,000 people worldwide including 8,500 across 9 sites in the UK. Our employees are not just part of a team—they are key contributors to shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.

SLR’s busy Mine Waste team has enjoyed continued commercial success across the globe in recent years. Recent changes in legislation and guidance, in the aftermath of the Brumadinho dam disaster in 2019, have seen a steep rise in the demand for consultancy services in relation to mine waste tailings dams. Consequently, we currently have an exciting opportunity for a senior grade engineer to join our mine waste team in Nottingham.
Our mine waste team provides specialist services to the mining industry across a wide range of areas related to the management of tailings and waste rock, from ground investigation, analysis of laboratory and monitoring data, design (conceptual to detailed) to construction supervision and quality assurance. In delivering this support, SLR uses state of the art software to evaluate saturated and unsaturated flow regimes; perform deformation analyses, stability analyses and stress / strain analyses, and modelling of soil structure interaction.
SLR is seeking a Graduate/Project Engineer to join our mine waste team in the UK, based in our Nottingham Office. This position will provide the successful candidate with a wide range of experience and is ideal for someone who is keen to develop their skills and knowledge in mining and civil engineering to become a chartered professional engineer.
The role would suit a graduate engineer, with an honours degree in either Civil or Mining Engineering or a Master’s degree in a related subject, such as Geotechnical Engineering.
The successful candidate will enjoy on-the-job training from a team of industry leading professionals, and will receive full support in working towards professional chartership with the ICE or IMMM.
The role
Provide office-based support to senior staff in the Nottingham office working on a range of mining projects.  The type of work will help develop this person towards chartered status and is envisaged to include the following:
• Support tendering activities / proposal writing
• Planning, procurement and management of site investigations
• Oversee installation of geotechnical instrumentation and monitoring of readings
• Numerical modelling
• Factual reporting
• Interpretive reporting
• Production of detailed designs and specifications
• Production of tender documents and bills of quantities
• Construction supervision
Whilst some projects will be based in the local area, the role may also involve supervision of projects in other locations throughout the UK and overseas for periods of up to 3 months at a time.
About us
SLR are global leaders in Sustainability Solutions, helping our clients achieve their sustainability goals. We are a consultancy with 4000+ employees across 6 regions in over 125 countries. Our ‘one team’ culture is at the heart of our business, providing a collaborative and supportive environment for professional development.
Along with competitive salaries, our staff enjoy a comprehensive benefits package with a company pension plus excellent healthcare offering, travel and life insurance and a structured career framework with regular reviews offering outstanding opportunities for progression. Alongside 25 day’s annual leave, with additional flexible bank holidays, we offer flexible, agile and hybrid working which enables staff to tailor hours worked around core hours, with family friendly policies help balance the needs of professional and home life.
About you
Essential:
• Minimum degree (BEng/BSc/MEng) in Geotechnical / Civil / Mining Engineering or other related engineering subject, or relevant MSc
• Graduate level ICE/IMMM membership or above (equivalent for overseas candidates)
• Good understanding of the principles of engineering and/or mining
• Appreciation of importance of a safe working environment
• Full UK driving license
• Good numerical skills are required.
• Good at both verbal and written communications.
• Flexibility to work away from home for extended periods of time.
• Willing to work on site in all conditions
• Motivated for Continued Professional Development (CPD)
• Embraces SLR’s ‘one-team’ culture
Desirable:
• Knowledge of numerical modelling using geotechnical package GeoStudio, Plaxis or any other industry standard software.
• Experience in using CAD, GIS and BIM.
• Knowledge of standard forms of contract, specifications and bills of quantities
• Graduate membership of either ICE or IMMM (or equivalent professional engineering governing body for overseas candidates)
• Can demonstrates previous examples where initiative has been used to solve a problem
• Can demonstrates previous examples of leadership
• Confidence to express an opinion and raise queries / concerns where appropriate
• Ability to lead on projects and when required instruct
• Willing to take on task outside of their normal role, such as organising / present at a lunch and learn
• Willingness to learn another language
Culture & Inclusion at SLR
We are committed to being an equal opportunities employer, and our expectations go beyond purely complying with legislation. Through our Regional C&I Committees, Global Council and Employee Networks, we foster an inclusive environment where all people regardless of their background can thrive.

To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.
Commercial Planning Analyst – UK
Please note, internally, this position is titled: Sr Forecast Analyst
Meet the team:
Join Dexcom's EMEA Commercial Forecasting & Analytics team and act as a strategic business partner to commercial leadership, providing data-driven forecasts and insights that inform key business decisions and shape how we bring life-changing diabetes technology to patients.
The numbers we put together don't just sit in a spreadsheet — they guide decisions across the business, from commercial planning and marketing to supply chain and investor relations. You will be working directly with senior leaders from day one, connecting the dots between strategy, insights and market trends, and turning them into a clear direction the business can act on.
If you enjoy understanding how markets evolve, solving complex business problems and translating uncertainty into actionable forecasts, you will feel right at home here.
Where you come in:
As Senior Commercial Forecasting Analyst, you’ll play a central role in leading both short-term and long-term revenue forecasting for Dexcom’s portfolio working closely with commercial teams, market access, operations and supply chain. You will be responsible for:
• Acting as a strategic partner for commercial leaders, providing insights and recommendations that support the identification of growth opportunities and risks, helping to shape the direction of the business
• Owning the quarterly revenue forecasting process and supporting the long-range planning (LRP) cycle across multiple regions
• Partnering with cross-functional stakeholders (analytics, pricing, commercial, marketing, market access…) to assess opportunities and risks, define robust forecast assumptions and align forecasts with strategic goals
• Presenting forecast assumptions and results to senior leadership, using clear, compelling and well-structured presentations and visualisations
• Leverage data to identify trends, growth drivers, and emerging risks, translating them into actionable insights that strengthen forecast quality and business planning
• Performing variance analysis to identify key performance drivers, explain changes versus expectations, and highlight emerging risks and opportunities
• Building scalable forecasting models and scenarios that help the business understand the impact of market dynamics and strategic decisions
• Drive continuous improvement of forecasting processes and methodologies to enhance business value, increase efficiency, and support the continued growth of the organisation
This role requires someone who’s not afraid to get your hands into the data, but who can also step back and think strategically. You’ll be joining a team where your insights will shape decisions — and where your enthusiasm and hunger to learn will be celebrated.
What makes you successful:
You’ll thrive in this role if you bring:
• Previous experience in Commercial Forecasting, Management Consulting, Commercial Analytics, FP&A, Business Planning, or a similar analytical or commercial function
• Strong business and commercial acumen, with the ability to understand market dynamics, identify growth opportunities and risks, and translate them into business recommendations
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to combine data, insights, and business priorities to support decision-making
• Excellent communication or storytelling skills in English, with the ability to present complex topics clearly and confidently to a range of stakeholders, including senior leadership
• A collaborative mindset. You are a team player with proven ability to build relationships, influence stakeholders, and work effectively across functions
• Experience building and maintain logical, scalable models in Excel
• Familiarity with VBA or other programming languages (e.g., SQL, R, Python, etc.) is an advantage, as well as accessing large data sets via Google BigQuery and Amazon Redshift
• Proactive and adaptable, comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment, with a growth mindset and a continuous focus on improvement and value creation
Nice to have
• Additional European languages such as German, Spanish, or French
• Familiarity with visualisation tools like Tableau or similar
• Experience in healthcare, medtech, pharmaceuticals, consulting, commercial operations, or related industries
What you’ll get:
• A front row seat to life changing CGM technology. Learn about our brave #dexcomwarriors community.
• A full and comprehensive benefits program.
• Growth opportunities on a global scale.
• Access to career development through in-house learning programs and/or qualified tuition reimbursement.
• An exciting and innovative, industry-leading organization committed to our employees, customers, and the communities we serve.

• 5-15%

• Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 5 – 8 years of related experience.

If you reside within commuting distance of a Dexcom site (typically 75 miles/120km) a hybrid working environment may be available. Ask about our Flex workplace option.

Leonardo offers a range of Apprenticeships from 2-4yrs. across a variety of STEM and business routes, offering paid training, coupled with on the job learning that enables you to gain practical skills, experience and knowledge that sets up the best start to your career. In addition you will work closely with work-based mentors to enable you to apply your academic knowledge within the work context. Security Clearance
At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years.  In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks.  Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

This is an exciting opportunity to join Airbus as an apprentice in the Structures Test Team at the Aerospace Integrated Research and Test Centre (AIRTeC) in Filton, Bristol. AIRTeC is a £100 million, state-of-the-art research and testing facility that supports Airbus’s advanced aircraft wing design and development.
The Structures Test Team is one of three key testing centres within Airbus, responsible for validating the strength and durability of cutting-edge materials and structural components used across all Airbus aircraft programmes, including next-generation, sustainable technologies like hydrogen propulsion, ultra-flexible wings, and blended wing body aircraft..
What will you be doing:
Year 1: During your first year you will spend Semester 1 (September to January) full-time studying at Weston College. In Semester 2 (February to June) you will start to spend 2 days per week onsite at Airbus Filton, with the other days at Weston college.
Years 2 and 3: Time to put your learning to action!
In second and third years, you will be on-site at Airbus Filton. Year 4: Apprentices will be based in their place of work on a full-time basis

• Cable manufacture and creation of bespoke connectors.
• Installing and commissioning control and data acquisition systems.

• Troubleshooting and repairing faulty equipment.
• Developing and optimising software-based calibration procedures.
• Ensuring compliance with quality management systems such as ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 17025.
• Supporting development of new calibration techniques and procedures.

• Build a blend of mechanical and electrical skills relevant to testing, calibration, and instrumentation.
• Develop professionally through structured training, academic learning, and hands-on projects.
As you progress, you’ll have the opportunity to specialise in areas aligned with your interests—whether that’s mechanical testing, data acquisition, or advanced calibration and metrology.

• Grade C or 4 in English

Working model: Hybrid (3 days in office per week)
Location: Building 12, Chiswick Business Park, 566 Chiswick High Road, London, W4 5AN
About the role
SEGA Europe’s Finance, Business Planning and Studio Finance teams are moving FP&A data, reporting and planning from fragmented, Excel-driven processes to governed, scalable CPM solutions. At the same time, these teams are changing how they work. We are looking for a finance-literate Project Manager to bring one consistent delivery standard to both – running the PMO for our CPM programme and data initiatives, driving process transformation, and making sure Finance processes are properly documented.
What you will do
PMO for the CPM programme and data-driven initiatives
• Plan and run delivery across a portfolio of concurrent initiatives – plans, milestones, dependencies, RAID, change control and status reporting.
• Keep progress transparent at all times: where each initiative stands, what is outstanding, who owns the next action, and what is needed to finish.
• Coordinate UAT, parallel testing, cutover and go-live with Finance, Business Planning, Studio Finance, IT, HR and implementation partners.
• Set and maintain PMO standards, templates and a single portfolio view; run the delivery cadence and steering committee packs.
• Support master data governance, including taking over the Title Master (our governed list of game titles) and its change control.
• Use AI tools to automate routine project management work, measure the time saved, and help colleagues adopt the same practices.
Process transformation
• Map the processes and handoffs affected by change, and plan the transition around the Finance calendar (month-end close, budget, forecast and mid-term planning).
• Identify adoption risks early; plan communications, training and readiness so new ways of working are adopted, not left to settle informally.
Process documentation
• Help Finance teams document their processes using the AI tools available, and keep that documentation current on a regular cycle.
• Make sure project, process and governance documents are complete, approved and easy to find, with decisions recorded when they are made.
• Reduce reliance on individual knowledge, so absence or handover never stalls an initiative.
What you will bring
• 5–8 years’ project management experience, including CPM/EPM, financial systems or finance transformation delivery.
• Solid understanding of the full finance cycle – financial accounting and month-end close as well as FP&A reporting, budgeting and forecasting.
• Experience running several initiatives at once in a matrix organisation, managing a wide range of stakeholders at different levels.
• Experience of process mapping, process documentation and supporting organisational change.
• Working knowledge of master data, hierarchies and change control; structured UAT and release management.
• Excellent organisational skills, with hands-on use of project management tools (e.g. Smartsheet, Jira/Confluence) to keep work on track and transparent.
• Hands-on experience using AI tools (e.g. Copilot, Claude, Smartsheet AI) to automate and optimise tasks.
• A confident facilitator who can influence without direct authority, stays calm under pressure and picks up new tools quickly.
• Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Nice to have
• CPM/EPM platforms (Vena, Anaplan, Adaptive, Hyperion); ERP systems such as Oracle; HRIS.
• PMP, PRINCE2, Agile or change management certification (e.g. Prosci); ACA, ACCA or CIMA (full or part-qualified).
• Experience in a global organisation, ideally in video games.
Working environment
London-based, hybrid: three days in the office and two days working from home.

We believe that making the best games relies on having the best people, so we make sure that we look after ours…
•
For our gaming buffs, you can get involved in our lunchtime get gaming sessions in our games lounge and Club SEGA, regular gaming tournaments and free SEGA games on Steam.

If you're more of a foodie, you can take advantage of fresh fruit and cereal every single day.

Fitness fanatics will love our discounted gym membership, ride to work scheme, workout area and bootcamps in the business park. You can find your zen with weekly yoga classes as well as in-house massage therapy.
•
You'll have access to a comprehensive benefits package that includes life assurance, income protection, private healthcare & dental insurance schemes and an enhanced contributory pension scheme. We offer competitive salaries and a fantastic bonus scheme so that you can stay motivated and focused on making SEGA the best it can be.
•
We hold regular lunch & learn sessions, company updates at incredible venues in Central London and Christmas parties that you’ll want to brag to your mates about! What’s not to love?
•
We pride ourselves on having flexible working hours to ensure that you have a life outside of the office.
•
We want people of all backgrounds to see themselves represented and included in our work, so we actively seek to diversify our team and bring more voices to the table. All applicants are welcome!

Through a combination of software, network, platform, DevOps, data, delivery and security placements, you will develop the knowledge and practical experience needed to design, build, deploy, operate and secure modern digital systems.
The starting salary for this role is £23,500 per annum.
The Role
Looking for a great start to your career in technology, earning and learning on a professionally accredited, award-winning scheme? We are recruiting the cyber, software, network, platform, DevOps, data and security professionals of the future on our nationally recognised, award-winning Degree Apprenticeship Programme.
Our Cyber Degree Apprenticeship is broader than a traditional cybersecurity programme. It provides experience across the disciplines involved in designing, building, testing, deploying, operating and securing modern digital systems.
This three-year programme combines Cyber Delivery (Engineering & Data) and Cyber Security, providing you with hands-on experience and a strong foundational skill set across engineering, data and security disciplines before you specialise in a chosen path.
During Years 1 and 2, you will complete a series of placements across key areas, including:
• Core Foundational Skills
• System Development (Software, Network, Platform, DevOps and Test)
• Data & Analytics (AI/ML, Data Engineering and Visualisation)
• Security Risk & Governance and Audit & Assurance
• Operational Security, including exposure to Security Operations Centres (SOC), threat detection, vulnerability management and incident response
• Cyber Project Delivery, providing an understanding of how multidisciplinary teams plan, coordinate and deliver cyber and digital projects
• Exposure to how Architecture supports secure system design, engineering and technical decision-making
In Year 3 you'll begin to specialise more in either Cyber Delivery or Cyber Security, having the opportunity to take on placements more focused on your chosen area and develop deeper expertise in preparation for a permanent role within the business.
Throughout your apprenticeship, you will:

• Detecting and remediating cyberattacks.
• Security design and architecture, security testing and response investigations.
• Risk analysis, governance and compliance.
• Understanding how cyber and digital projects are planned and delivered.
• Engage in STEM outreach and community initiatives.

Your work will support critical business areas throughout Leonardo and our customers in the UK government and private sector and will provide you with great learning opportunities in the field. At the same time, you will obtain the academic knowledge and qualifications necessary for your future career in a high-tech company through your course at one of our partner universities.
You will be working within world-class facilities, in both office and lab environments and will have opportunities to travel to other Leonardo UK and customer sites, to meet with colleagues, customers, and suppliers.
Beyond the programme there may be the opportunity for you to further your academic and vocational achievements based on your talents and capability and needs of the business. You would be expected to commit to the successful completion of all your academic modules and assignments in support of the Apprenticeship standard.
What We’re Looking For
This Apprenticeship assumes little prior cybersecurity experience and is NOT suitable for candidates who already have an engineering, software or computing degree.

• 3 A-Levels (Grades A–C)
•
• One must be in Mathematics and another in Physics or an Engineering/Technology/IT related subject.
OR
• BTEC Extended Diploma in Engineering (with maths bridging course).
Plus:
• 5 GCSEs (Grades 9–4 / A*–C) including English, Maths, and a Science subject.
We consider each application individually in consultation with our partnering university.
Security Clearance
At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations.  As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.
For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV).  As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.
To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. The opportunity:
Our Central London team is looking for talented and enthusiastic modelling and simulation practitioners to create and integrate weapon system models for our UK Ministry of Defence (MOD) customer. The role will suit either recent STEM graduates, postgraduates, or those with relevant industry experience of engineering models who wish to apply their abilities in an aerospace modelling and simulation environment. This is intended as a fulltime position, but we would consider part time working of 4 days per week.
• Role includes a 12.% Salary Uplift.
The type of project will you be working on:
• Customer Integration: You will be a member of a weapons project team within our larger Defence Analytics Group working in Central London. The group is integrated into a joint unit with government employees, members of the armed forces, and other contractors.
• The Challenge: To create dynamic computer models for internal and external simulation environments to assess the performance and capability of weapon systems. Complex systems are modelled primarily in MATLAB/Simulink, exercised to answer customer questions, and exported for integration into customers’ modelling environments.
• Collaboration: You will be working in close liaison with teams within the UK and partner nations, with the opportunity to contribute, influence, challenge and improve joint ways of working and knowledge.
• Breadth: You will be working in an environment where both the complexity and capabilities of the systems are continually evolving throughout the world.
What you’ll do as a Defence Analytics Engineer:
• Produce computer models of weapons systems, exercise them in-house, and aid the integration of these models in customers’ simulation environments.
• Produce reports and presentations of your work and present them to local MOD customers and the wider community both within the UK and partner nations.
• Provide ad hoc advice and support to MOD customers, often at short notice.
• Use your developing experience and knowledge to propose and implement improvements to tools and processes.
• In conjunction with the project team conduct regular liaison with both MOD and the wider customer base to keep them informed of recent developments and to determine future analysis requirements.
• Seek co-operative and collaborative approaches with our UK and multi-national partners, identifying best practice.
• Travel for technical exchanges with our partners, in the UK and abroad.
What we need from you:
• A good understanding of scientific methods and their use through the application of fundamental physical principles.
• A degree in a STEM subject and strong numerical and analytical skills, with the ability to apply these to real world problems through modelling and simulation.
• Knowledge of aerospace technologies such as aerodynamics, propulsion, sensors, guidance and control would be an advantage.
• Experience in some of the following programming languages: MATLAB/Simulink, C/C++, C# and/or Python.
• Good interpersonal skills which allow you to work collaboratively and effectively within an inter-disciplinary team.
• Ability to problem solve and self-steer work to deadlines as necessary, sometimes at short notice.
• Ability to communicate, both in writing and verbally, with audiences of differing technical backgrounds and seniority.
It would be nice if you had:
• Experience of defence modelling and simulation environments, customers and requirements would be an advantage.
What you will get:
• Impact: You will help ensure that MOD’s weapon assessments are robust and delivered in a timely manner to UK Defence partners and front-line forces. This will be in the form of computer models and product generated from these models.
• Opportunity: To play a key role in MOD weapon assessment which is a critical input to MOD’s equipment procurement programs.
• Knowledge: You will develop a detailed understanding of weapon systems and how they operate, and how to encapsulate that understanding and assessment in a dynamic computer model.
• Skills: You will develop a range of analytical, software and interpersonal skills.
• Insights: Working within a Leonardo team that is fully integrated with its MOD customer will provide an excellent opportunity to see up-close how the MOD operates and interacts with its customers and partners.
• Teamwork: You will work with a diverse technical team in a highly collaborative, multi-national environment.
• Delegation: It is expected that you will steer tasks, processes and improvement initiatives.

Role Title: Containment Fault Studies Analyst
We are Rolls‑Royce SMR and we’re doing something that’s never been done before. We’re revolutionising an industry. That’s a once‑in‑a‑career opportunity for those excited by such a challenge. This is more than just a job; this is a legacy.
About the Team:
The Performance & Analysis team is the centre of excellence within Rolls‑Royce SMR for the engineering analysis used to substantiate the performance and safety of the power station.
Multiple opportunities are available across thermal hydraulic plant performance and safety analysis, including reactor plant transient and fault analysis, core sub-channel analysis and containment analysis. The team provides the technical evidence needed to support design decisions, safety case development and regulatory compliance across the SMR programme.
About the Role:
As a Containment Fault Studies Analyst, you will model the thermal-hydraulic behaviour of containment systems and their associated emergency cooling systems.
You will develop engineering models and analyses that demonstrate the effectiveness of containment and safety systems during faulted conditions, using the results to support design optimisation and the substantiation of nuclear safety claims. Analysis outputs form a key part of the safety case and contribute directly to the verification and validation of the SMR design.
You will work closely with design engineers, safety specialists, performance analysts and test teams, helping to define analysis requirements and communicate results across a wide range of technical disciplines.
We’ll Need You To:
• Develop and execute thermal-hydraulic containment analyses
• Model containment performance and emergency cooling system behaviour
• Assess plant operation during: Normal operating conditions Operational transients Reactor fault scenarios
• Support the substantiation of containment and safety system performance
• Produce technical reports and safety case contributions
• Develop and maintain analysis methods, models and tools
• Support code verification, validation and uncertainty quantification activities

• Experience using industry-standard thermal hydraulic analysis software
• Experience producing technical analysis reports and supporting safety case documentation
• Experience with tools such as RELAP, FLOMASTER, VIPRE, CTF, GOTHIC or similar would be advantageous

• Experience developing analysis tools and scripts, ideally using Python
• Understanding of multidisciplinary and coupled analysis approaches

• Ability to explain complex analytical results clearly

• Strong stakeholder engagement and collaboration skills

• Chartered Engineer (or equivalent) desirable

Caretaker

Make a practical difference, every day

We are a crowdfunded company and have a dedicated and enthusiastic community of backers who are helping us create the “Best Damn Space Sim Ever”. We want to build the best we can deliver and we believe wholeheartedly in the value of exceptional diverse talent.
Founded in 2012 by renowned game developer Chris Roberts, Cloud Imperium Games (CIG) is one of the largest global independent studios, dedicated to delivering next-generation AAA games. CIG prides itself in thinking outside the box, encouraging creativity and developing ground-breaking technology. CIG believes in raising the bar for the gaming industry and the gaming community as a whole.
About the Role
As a Senior Lighting Artist at CIG, you will be joining a team responsible for lighting all the amazing locations in Star Citizen.  Star Citizen is a universe filled with solar systems, each of which are filled with diverse locations all of which the player can seamlessly fly down to from space and explore on foot.
In this senior position, you will take ownership of implementing and overseeing high-quality, complex, and cinematic realtime lighting scenarios for Star Citizen. This could be anything from a moody old Space Station in low orbit around a planet to a neon-filled cityscape located on a planet. The art pillars of the game are Cinematic Sci-Fi Realism. You will play a pivotal role in establishing the mood, tone, and visual quality for environments, ensuring the final frame showcases the artwork to the highest possible industry standard.
This is an onsite role based at our studio in Manchester, UK.
Check out what our Lighting team get up to:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cqt1fl56BlE&t=1s
What does a Senior Lighting Artist at CIG do?
• Create and champion believable, cinematic and narrative-driven lighting scenarios for major locations in the game.
• Optimise and ensure complex lighting setups work seamlessly within strict defined realtime rendering budgets, proactively identifying performance bottlenecks.
• Work closely with the Lighting Lead and Art Director to interpret, execute, and help maintain the overall artistic vision across the project.
• Collaborate deeply with other departments (Environment Art, Tech Art, Design) to pioneer workflows and help create the best player experience possible.
• Act as a technical and artistic resource for junior and mid-level artists, helping elevate the team’s collective skillset.
What do we expect from our Senior Lighting Artists?
• Extensive experience in creating high-quality, AAA realtime lighting scenarios, with a strong portfolio showcasing a masterful handle on mood and composition.
• Someone who is deeply passionate about creating inspirational lighting moods and storytelling through light.
• Deep understanding of material shading, physically based rendering (PBR), and how the interplay of different materials impacts the final frame under varying light conditions.
• A profound knowledge of cinematic lighting principles (composition, colour theory, exposure) combined with the technical know-how to implement them in a cutting-edge engine.

JET's Information Security organisation protects a technology-led, cloud-native platform serving millions of customers across multiple markets.
JET's Security Governance function sets the standards that keep a large, cloud-native technology organisation secure and compliant. These are some of the key components to the position:

• Track exceptions and remediation plans with technical owners, escalating risks where needed and maintaining visibility across the Three Lines of Defence.

What will you bring to the team?
• Solid hands-on experience in Information Security GRC within a technology-led or cloud-first organisation, with a track record of keeping governance frameworks operational at pace.
• Working knowledge of security control frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001) and how they apply to modern engineering environments including cloud infrastructure, microservices, and DevOps.
• Proven ability to coordinate across the Three Lines of Defence translating audit and compliance requirements into clear, actionable tasks for engineering teams without creating unnecessary friction.
• Clear communicator who can explain governance requirements and control expectations to both technical engineers and non-technical risk or business stakeholders.
• Organised and delivery-focused, with the ability to manage multiple governance workstreams, track remediation through to closure, and keep processes running in a fast-moving organisation.
• Data-driven approach to compliance tracking comfortable building dashboards, spotting trends in control data, and surfacing the right information to support leadership decisions.

Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.

Job Title
Data Privacy Manager
Job Description
Data Privacy Manager
About IG Group
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
About the Role
IG's Data & AI team is scaling up how the business governs, understands, and trusts its data. As our Data Privacy Manager, you'll be the Group's central point of contact for data privacy - closing the gap between policy and practice, taking ownership of the RoPA process, DPIAs, DSAR protocol, retention practices, and breach reporting, and giving IG a single accountable home for data privacy compliance.
About the Team
This role sits within the Data & AI team, reporting into the Head of Data Governance & Strategy. This is an individual contributor role and the first hire into a newly centralised function, so it requires someone comfortable working on their own initiative and building relationships with stakeholders at all levels. As the function scales, this role will pick up direct reports.
Key Responsibilities
As Data Privacy Manager, you'll lead the strategic and day-to-day agenda for data privacy at IG, partnering closely with Legal, Risk, Compliance, HR, Procurement, Technology, and Product colleagues. You'll help evolve a privacy capability that is rigorous where it needs to be and practical everywhere it can be.
• Be the central point of contact for data privacy - act as the go-to for all data privacy related questions across the Group, from policy interpretation to practical guidance for staff at all levels.
• Support the governance framework - support the development of the data privacy governance framework, from DPIAs and privacy by design to retention, RoPA and third-party diligence.
• Own cross-border data transfers - put in place and maintain the mechanisms that allow personal data to move lawfully between IG's UK, EU and international entities, such as Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement, and adequacy assessments.
• Own the regulatory interface - manage breach notifications to the relevant regulator within the required regulatory timeframe, DPIA consultations, and centralised data privacy reporting to SLT/Board.
• Advise on privacy by design - advise product and business teams on the privacy implications of new products, changes and customer journeys.
• Translate law into practical guidance - translate UK privacy law into clear, proportionate recommendations that enable responsible decisions.
• Manage complex privacy incidents - including regulatory notification and engagement with affected individuals where required.
• Strengthen privacy awareness - across the business and help build out the privacy function as it grows - running training programmes that go beyond policy awareness to cover breach recognition and escalation for all staff.
• Contribute to the Group's approach to data risk - across a broad range of business activity.
Role Requirements
• 5+ years' experience - in a dedicated data privacy role within a regulated environment.
• Strong working knowledge of UK GDPR and EU GDPR - together with practical awareness of other privacy regimes relevant to IG's international footprint, including practical experience running DPIAs, RoPA and DSAR processes end-to-end.
• Experience operating within a multi-jurisdictional group structure - (e.g. UK, EU, APAC).
• Experience designing and embedding privacy governance documentation - policies, procedures, and escalation routes, ideally in an organisation without an existing dedicated function.
• Comfortable acting as the primary point of contact - for regulators, and for internal Audit and Risk stakeholders, on data privacy matters.
• Strong communication skills - able to translate legal and regulatory requirements into practical guidance for Product, Technology, HR, and other business teams.
• Experience delivering data privacy training and awareness programmes.
Desirable
• Experience in UK financial services or a similarly regulated industry.
• Practical exposure to AI/ML-related privacy considerations - (e.g. automated decision-making, Article 22).
• Professional certification in data protection/privacy - (e.g. CIPP/E, CIPM, BCS Certificate in Data Protection).
The Perks
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.
• Competitive salary
• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days
• A comprehensive global and local onboarding process
• Enhanced primary (maternity), secondary (paternity), and shared parental pay and leave, as well as a range of support and benefits for parents
Learn more about the Perks here!

Job Details:
Job Description:
Altera develops world-class Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) technology which comprises both the FPGA hardware itself and the associated software components, including tools for High-Level Design (HLD) entry.
The two major Altera HLD tools are DSP Builder (based on MATLAB/Simulink) and HLS which are built on a common HLD compiler stack. The HLD compiler generates highly-optimised FPGA RTL including automatic device mapping and pipelining. DSP Builder and HLS users can therefore focus on the architecture of their design without needing to spend time writing and re-writing RTL.
Altera is looking for engineers to join our teams. As a member of the UK DSP Builder team within the HLD group, you will be responsible for:
•
developing and supporting DSP Builder
•
designing and implementing improvements in the HLD compiler stack.
Your work will include:
•
analysis of bottlenecks in user designs and the corresponding implementation of compiler optimizations
•
comprehensive benchmarking of the FPGA-targeted generated hardware. As optimization is a global problem, the work may involve a mix of compiler software development and digital hardware design.
UK Altera office is in Marlow, 40 minutes from central London and Oxford.

Masters Degree or five years commercial experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or related fields

Strong software skills using C/C++, including working knowledge of efficient data structures and algorithms
•
Technical knowledge and appreciation of digital hardware design concepts
•
Good problem solving skills
•
Good interpersonal and communication skills

Experience with digital hardware design using Verilog/VHDL and related design flows

As a Lead Graphics Programmer in the Manchester Studio, you would be pushing forwards the rendering technology that powers a huge sandbox universe, spanning every conceivable scale from shading interstellar gas clouds, planets and asteroid belts, down to rendering individual human hairs.
You will also advance the core rendering technology that aspires to achieve photo-real visuals, such as physically based light, eye and lens simulations, as well as more low-level engine technologies such as shader building & compilation, content streaming systems, and the multi-threaded and cross-API renderer architecture.

Founded in 2012, Cloud Imperium Games creates cutting-edge videogames that defy expectations. We’re currently developing Star Citizen, a record-breaking multiplayer online space sim, and Squadron 42, a cinematic single-player adventure set in the same universe.
What does a Lead Graphics Programmer at Cloud Imperium Games do?
In short, on a daily basis you will:
• Lead the technical direction of graphics and rendering systems within your domain.
• Drive research and implementation of new cutting-edge graphics technology and tools.
• Own major rendering features and systems from design through to delivery and long-term maintenance.
• Analyse, refactor and improve upon existing graphics technology.
• Manage a team of graphics programmers, including performance reviews, development planning, and day-to-day support.
• Coordinate workload and priorities within the graphics team in collaboration with production and engineering leadership.
• Work closely with art, design, and engineering teams to align visual goals with technical solutions.
• Assist and advise other software developers in use of graphics/rendering features, while debugging and fixing complex problems.
• Profile and optimise the entire rendering pipeline, including lighting and shading components of the game.
• Help define technical standards, workflows, and performance targets for the rendering team.
• Keep up to date with the latest graphics and rendering techniques and tools, helping us to innovate, plan, and deliver full features.
What do we expect from our Lead Graphics Programmers?
• Expert-level C++ skills in a large shared codebase, including architecture, code reviews, and performance-critical systems.
• Strong experience with shader languages and modern graphics APIs.
• Deep knowledge of 3D rendering, 3D math, and optimisation of the complete rendering pipeline.
• Proven experience owning significant graphics or engine-level systems.
• Experience managing engineers, including performance management and career development.
• Strong software debugging skills to effectively track, diagnose and solve complex issues.
• Work well in a cooperative, cross-functional team environment; ability to translate technical jargon to non-technical audiences.

Looking for a Veterinary Surgeon role where you can enjoy a varied caseload, develop your clinical confidence and learn from experienced colleagues? With a varied mix of consulting, surgery and hospital work, an impressive range of diagnostic equipment and a genuine commitment to professional development, this is an opportunity to build your experience in a collaborative environment, with the added benefit of a four-day working pattern in a typical week.
Why join us?
• A varied, flexible clinical role: a mix of consulting, operating and dedicated hospital inpatient shifts, with the opportunity to tailor your working week to your clinical interests.
• A four-day working pattern: typically four 9-hour days per week, with a structured weekend rota and no routine out-of-hours duties.

Cromwell Veterinary Group is centred around its RCVS-accredited hospital in Huntingdon, supported by five surrounding branch practices. Together, they offer a varied first-opinion caseload and access to a broad network of clinical expertise, creating opportunities to learn from colleagues across a wide range of disciplines.
Our hospital is exceptionally well equipped to support the investigation and treatment of a broad range of cases in-house. Facilities include digital radiography and a brand-new ultrasound machine with five probes, including three cardiac probes. We also have rhinoscopy, bronchoscopy, gastroscopy and laparoscopy equipment, alongside a veterinary orthopaedic kit, giving our clinicians access to a range of diagnostic and surgical capabilities.
Our in-house laboratory is equally well stocked, with EPOC, in-house coagulation testing, IDEXX ProCyte, Catalyst and SediVue analysers, as well as Antech HESKAView for digital cytology. These facilities support timely diagnostics and varied clinical work, providing opportunities to build your diagnostic skills and explore areas of clinical interest.
One of Cromwell's greatest strengths is its people. Our team of 24 Veterinary Surgeons includes certificate holders and Advanced Practitioners across medicine, soft tissue surgery, orthopaedics, cardiology, emergency and critical care, ophthalmology, oncology, diagnostic imaging and dentistry. Clinical discussions and shared learning are an important part of hospital life, giving you access to a wealth of knowledge as you continue developing your own skills.
The role involves a mix of consulting days, operating days and dedicated hospital inpatient shifts, with the opportunity to tailor the balance to your clinical interests. You'll work closely with experienced Registered Veterinary Nurses and our dedicated Client Care team, managing a varied caseload while benefiting from the support of the wider hospital team. Some flexibility is required to provide cover at surrounding branches where necessary.
We're also committed to supporting your continued development. You'll receive a £1,500 CPD allowance and 40 hours of CPD leave, with additional support available for Advanced Practitioners. Alongside monthly in-house CPD and structured clinical rounds, you'll have opportunities to learn from colleagues, share knowledge and continue developing your clinical interests.
Our dedicated twilight and night veterinary teams provide continuity of inpatient care around the clock. Rather than patients being transferred elsewhere overnight, patients can remain at Cromwell, cared for by a team that knows their case. This helps us maintain continuity, communication and high standards of patient care throughout their stay.
The working pattern is designed around a four-day week in a typical week, averaging 40 hours across the rota. Weekend duties are structured across a 12-week rota block, with time off in lieu built into the schedule. There are no routine out-of-hours duties for day vets.
Located in the heart of Cambridgeshire, Huntingdon offers a great balance between town and country living, with Cambridge within easy reach. Good road and rail connections make commuting straightforward from Peterborough, St Neots, Bedford and surrounding areas, while the local countryside provides plenty of opportunities to enjoy your time away from work.

We're looking for a Veterinary Surgeon who enjoys first-opinion practice, takes pride in delivering excellent patient care and wants to continue developing their clinical skills as part of a collaborative team.
• RCVS registration.
• At least two years' experience in UK small-animal practice post GDP.
• Confidence managing a varied first-opinion caseload.
• Strong communication and relationship-building skills with a collaborative approach to clinical decision-making.
An interest in pursuing further qualifications or certificates would be welcomed, but is by no means essential. Most importantly, we're looking for someone who wants to contribute to a supportive clinical team while continuing to grow in their own practice.

About the job
The Role
This a portfolio-level regulatory strategy role covering regions with diverse regulatory requirements and market dynamics: APAC, LATAM, MEA, CIS, Adriatics and Partner Business Regions. Working with the Therapeutic Area Lead, you'll set regional regulatory strategy for a defined product portfolio — not just chasing individual approvals, but shaping the pathway decisions, life cycle management, and health authority relationships that determine how well global strategy actually lands on the ground.
Location: Maidenhead/Hybrid, 3-days a week on-site
Why It Matters
A global regulatory strategy depends on strong regional insights across all markets. These regions do not follow the same dynamics as the US or EU — different evidentiary bars, different timelines, different risk calculus — and getting that wrong costs approval time and access. This role owns that judgment: turning global strategy into regionally credible submissions and pushing regional intelligence back up into global thinking before it becomes a problem rather than after.
What You'll Be Responsible For
You'll act as the regional regulatory strategist for your product portfolio, balancing scientific rigor with the practical realities of dozens of different regulatory systems, while building the relationships — internal and external — that make timely approval possible.
• Develop and implement regional regulatory strategies aligned to global priorities, identifying the most efficient approval pathways with input from Local Regulatory Responsible (LRR) and Regulatory Partner Representative (RPR) colleagues
• Contribute to Global Regulatory Strategy activities, including planning and responding to complex scientific questions requiring product expertise and cross-functional input
• Provide strategic oversight of submissions — marketing applications, life cycle management, tender applications, and PSURs — anticipating regulatory risk before it becomes a delay
• Ensure high-quality submission documentation and health authority responses, delivered on schedule and to regional requirements
• Build and sustain strong working relationships with LRRs, RPRs, internal stakeholders, and regional health authorities themselves
• Stay current on international legislation and guidance relevant to CSL's products and initiatives, including rare disease, orphan drug, toll manufacturing, and reliance pathway considerations
Experience Required
• Substantial experience in regulatory affairs within pharma or biotech, with direct exposure to APAC, LATAM, or comparable emerging-market regulatory environments
• A degree in Biological or Medical Science or Pharmacy, preferably with a post-graduate qualification
• Demonstrated ability to develop and execute regional regulatory strategy in alignment with global product strategy
• Strong working knowledge of marketing application, life cycle management, and PSUR/reporting requirements across multiple jurisdictions
• Experience engaging directly with health authorities, with a track record of clear, credible communication that supports positive outcomes
• Comfort operating as a subject matter expert — assessing regulatory impact, identifying risk, and advising cross-functional teams accordingly
• A collaborative style suited to matrixed, multi-stakeholder environments, with the judgment to prioritize across a live portfolio
• English is mandatory, while additional language skill would be an asset (e.g. Arabic, French, Spanish, Russian)

With state-of-the-art production facilities in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia, CSL Seqirus utilizes egg, cell and adjuvant technologies to offer a broad portfolio of differentiated influenza vaccines in more than 20 countries around the world.

Senior Embedded Software Developer
The opportunity
Make Unity run everywhere! That is the mantra of the Embedded OS Platforms team. Users expect stunning interactive experiences everywhere: from in-car infotainment systems and digital cockpits to touch-screen kiosks in showrooms and at sporting events. Unity is at the forefront with our scalable, performant runtime engine and Unity Editor workflow.
We are looking for a senior software engineer to join our growing team. The team builds and supports the Unity versions that run on Embedded platforms, like Embedded Linux, QNX and Android Automotive OS. As UX evolves to include multiple screens, layering of 3D content with other applications and rich multi-touch input, our platform grows to match expectations.
Unity is committed to solving the hardest technical challenges, and this role plays a key part in delivering industry solutions for our customers. You will work with teams across Unity, including industry teams who work directly with customers and R&D teams responsible for cross-platform support, systems architecture, libraries, as well as runtime optimization.
What success looks like
In your first 3-6 months, you've ramped up on one of our embedded platforms, shipped your first integrations and bug fixes, and become a trusted contributor in customer-facing investigations.
Within 12 months, you own a meaningful area of a platform (e.g. AAOS integration) its performance on constrained embedded SoCs and act as a technical point of contact for one of our customers. You guide team wide initiatives with your experience and expertise.
Your impact
You'll be part of a small, senior team with a strong impact. The code you write ships in production vehicles, and your work directly unblocks Unity's embedded and automotive business. You'll help define the technical bar across the team and shape how Unity supports the next generation of software-defined vehicles.
Why you'll love it
Genuinely hard problems at the frontier of Real Time 3D and embedded systems. Contribution to cutting edge automotive HMI experiences. A diverse range of responsibilities spanning feature work and customer support. Real ownership, agency and opportunities to grow in a small and senior team that turns the needle and moves the industry forward.
What you'll be doing
•
Bring Unity's Real Time 3D runtime to embedded platforms, like Embedded Linux, QNX and Android Automotive OS, developing new features and integrations that address the needs of industries like the automotive HMI market.
•
Integrate Unity into native Android apps (e.g. via Unity Render Service) and build the graphics and windowing layer that powers multi-screen, multi-touch digital cockpits and HMIs.
•
Profile and optimize KPI like runtime performance, memory, startup/load time and iteration speed of Unity for resource-constrained embedded SoCs across platforms.
•
Partner directly with customers like automotive OEMs as a technical point of contact, investigating issues, removing performance bottlenecks, and setting customers up for production success.
•
Raise the engineering bar for a small and senior team through design discussions, code reviews, and automated testing .
What we're looking for
•
Languages: Proficiency in C/C++/C\# and building scalable feature sets in a large multithreaded codebase.
•
Embedded Platforms: Experience developing for Embedded Linux, QNX and hypervised environments
•
Android platform: Hands-on AAOS or AOSP development experience on the platform layer, experience integrating into the Android lifecycle as well as using the Android compositing stack (SurfaceFlinger, HWComposer, Gralloc, EGL).
•

Ready for a challenge?
Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.
Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.
About this role
JET's Security Architecture & Engineering function is responsible for making data protection a built-in property of how we design and operate our platforms, not an afterthought. As Data Security Specialist, you'll be responsible for engineering the controls that safeguard JET's most sensitive structured and unstructured data across cloud-native and enterprise environments. You'll translate architectural data security standards into working, scalable implementations  from DLP platforms to encryption pipelines, and embed Privacy and Security by Design into engineering delivery.
You'll work at the intersection of data security engineering and automation, engineering to turn continuous insights like data security findings into automated engineering guardrails. Utilising CI/CD pipelines, and LLM-driven automation, your vision will enhance our automated data defense, your execution will deliver continuous compliance and risk reduction, and your approach will care deeply about creating frictionless security workflows that enable development teams to innovate safely. Together with engineering, IT, and business stakeholders, you'll drive a culture where security isn't a hurdle, it's a competitive advantage that helps us win together.
These are some of the key components to the position:
• Support and work with the team on JET's Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) and Data Loss Prevention (DLP)  program.
• Contribute and work on program goals aligned to internal policies and technical standards.
• Tune data security controls and DLP policies, triage findings, manage false positives and rule exceptions, and maintain a low false positive rate.
• Working with business stakeholders and data owners on all aspects of the DSPM and DLP program.
• Advise data owners and work alongside engineering teams, providing clear technical documentation and developer-friendly data protection tools to ensure the security and integrity of JET data while continuing to enable the business to operate at pace.
• Contribute to data security posture metrics and reporting, including classification coverage, exposure remediation SLAs, and DLP false positive rates.
What will you bring to the team?
• Experience implementing and managing data security controls in cloud-native or SaaS environments, spanning DSPM platforms (e.g., Wiz), SaaS-native DLP (e.g., Google Workspace, Slack), and data classification programs
• Experience working with structured and unstructured data discovery and classification techniques (e.g., pattern matching, regex, NLP-based scanning).
• A good understanding of encryption and cryptography principles as they apply to data security (knowledge of what to use, when to use it, and how it's applied).
• Comfortable utilising AI and setting up automations to parse, prioritise, and fine-tune alerts and findings.
• Experience with Terraform and ideally some scripting experience (Python)
• Ability to translate security goals and objectives into working technical solutions.
• Understanding of governance policies and technical standards and the ability to translate these into technical solutions, checklists, and actionable items for data owners and the wider business.
• Demonstrable experience collaborating and building trusted partnerships across DevOps, Software Engineering, IT, Data Owners, and Privacy teams, acting as an enabler rather than a blocker
• Understanding and experience applying full DSPM & DLP lifecycle in an enterprise environment
• Understanding of data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) with a strong ethical foundation, upholding standards for the secure handling of highly sensitive structured and unstructured data
• Ability to be pragmatic and work proactively in a fast-paced enterprise environment, owning your results
At JET, this is how we play
Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.
Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.
At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.
Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.
Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging
No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.
What else are we delivering?
Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET journeys.
Are you ready to join the team? Apply now!
