LSEG is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with significant operations in 65 countries across EMEA, North America, Latin America and Asia Pacific. We employ 26,000 people globally, more than half located in Asia Pacific. LSEG’s ticker symbol is LSEG.
OUR PEOPLE:
People are at the heart of what we do and drive the success of our business. Our values of Integrity, Partnership, Excellence and Change shape how we think, how we do things and how we help our people fulfil their potential. We embrace diversity and actively seek to attract individuals with unique backgrounds and perspectives. We break down barriers and encourage teamwork, enabling innovation and rapid development of solutions that make a difference. Our workplace generates an enriching and rewarding experience for our people and customers alike. Our vision is to build an inclusive culture in which everyone feels encouraged to fulfil their potential.
We know that real personal growth cannot be achieved by simply climbing a career ladder – which is why we encourage and enable a wealth of avenues and interesting opportunities for everyone to broaden and deepen their skills and expertise. As a global organisation spanning 65 countries and one rooted in a culture of growth, opportunity, diversity and innovation, LSEG is a place where everyone can grow, develop and fulfil your potential with meaningful careers.
ABOUT FTSE Russell, a division of LSEG
FTSE Russell is a global index leader that provides innovative benchmarking, analytics and data solutions for investors worldwide. FTSE Russell calculates thousands of indexes that measure and benchmark markets and asset classes in more than 70 countries, covering 98% of the investable market globally.
FTSE Russell index expertise and products are used extensively by institutional and retail investors globally. Approximately $17.9 trillion is currently benchmarked to FTSE Russell indexes. For over 30 years, leading asset owners, asset managers, ETF providers and investment banks have chosen FTSE Russell indexes to benchmark their investment performance and create ETFs, structured products and index-based derivatives.
ROLE PROFILE
The Head of Strategic Accounts EMEA (Sales Division), will lead the group focusing on significant accounts which involve large Asset Managers mainly focusing on developing and running passively managed products (ETFs, Mandates, Index Funds…). The role is to work alongside various teams like product, marketing, SI, PR and to develop the existing book of business by getting to know these firms at various levels. The role involves:
• The development of the FTSE Russell Asset-based Index business as well as the Data & Subscription side, accelerating revenue growth.
• Partnering with clients to launch new investment and derivative products linked to FTSE Russell indices through in-house development and index partnerships
• Delivering strategic Index solutions to clients and partner with them to design innovative new indices / Fostering regular conversations to create new ideas
• Partnering with clients in Asset-gathering campaigns to grow Index AUM and trading volume in Index derivatives
• Developing the Index ecosystem and positioning FTSE Russell as strategic solutions partner
ROLE SUMMARY
Reporting directly to the Head of EMEA Sales (FTSE Russell), the Head of Strategic Accounts EMEA will play a key leadership role within the regional team and having responsibility for driving Index adoption within the ETF Providers’ community (Global and Regional Asset Managers) and the development of Index solutions in the Asset Management space across ETFs, Mutual Funds and Segregated Accounts. In addition, this role will have accountability for developing and leading the Buy-Side regional strategy for asset-based index solutions. You will engage with the FTSE Russell’s Buy-Side side clients in the region and work in close collaboration & coordination with colleagues in Sales, Product Management, Research and marketing to drive revenue growth of FTSE Russell indices.
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:
Key aspects of the role include encouraging product adoption and education, as well as AUM growth for passive index investment products. The candidate will work closely with the senior clients providing key consultative solutions and focused relationships at all levels.
The role will involve all aspects of business management & development, strategy formulation, team leadership, client engagement and relationship management and internal coordination across the regional team and working closely with the other regions to ensure global consistency.
The role is a player-coach role, directly leading client relationships, strategy and business development with top clients and also leading a team of individuals covering asset managers to help guide, coach and develop individuals with development plans to drive asset-based growth for the index business.
The individual will be responsible for a broad range of activities:
• Set the strategic priorities for the Buy-side coverage within your region in alignment with broader business objectives to promote growth of asset-based revenue across the index ecosystem.
• Set team objectives and KPIs, training requirements, development plans, performance reviews
• Develop and lead on execution of the strategic growth plans to increase FTSE Russell index adoption and market penetration for the Buy-side segment.
• Have direct responsibility for leading major client relationships, setting strategy and executing on plans.

The Senior Quantity Surveyor supports construction project delivery by monitoring progress through the measurement and evaluation of installed quantities against approved plans and baselines. The role integrates quantity tracking, forecasting, and estimate loading with cost and performance metrics, contributing to value engineering, cost-benefit analysis, and feasibility assessments across labour, materials, and execution strategies. Working under general direction, the position applies specialised project controls knowledge to interpret complex issues, maintain accurate MTO data from IFC drawings, and support informed decision-making. The role also provides guidance to less experienced team members while ensuring delivery is aligned with organisational policies, procedures, and business objectives.

•
Monitor construction progress through detailed measurement and evaluation of installed quantities against approved plans and baseline estimates
•
Maintain and update quantity take-offs and material take-offs (MTOs) based on Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings to support accurate progress tracking
•
Develop and maintain forecasting models, including estimate loading and cost projections aligned with project schedules and delivery milestones
•
Perform cost-benefit analysis, value engineering assessments, and feasibility studies to optimise labour, materials, and execution strategies
•
Analyse variances between planned and actual quantities and provide insights to support corrective actions and commercial decisions
•
Contribute to project controls reporting by integrating quantity, cost, and progress data into standard reporting deliverables
•
Interpret internal and external project issues, applying technical expertise to develop practical solutions and best practices
•
Coordinate with cross-functional stakeholders including engineering, planning, and commercial teams to ensure data consistency and alignment
•
Provide guidance to less experienced team members and support prioritisation of workload across project deliverables
•
Support compliance with company policies, procedures, and project governance frameworks in all quantity surveying activities
Experience Required
Essential
•
Previous experience in quantity surveying within construction, EPC, or infrastructure projects
•
Proven experience with quantity tracking, measurement, and progress reporting on large-scale projects
•
Experience developing forecasts, cost estimates, and project controls reporting
•
Experience interpreting and working from Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings
•
Experience in value engineering and cost analysis within project delivery environments
Desirable
•
Experience working within integrated project controls environments
•
Knowledge of earned value management and cost control methodologies
•

Senior Clinical Statistical Programmer (Portfolio Development / Biometrics / Programming)
The Role
CSL is looking for a Senior Programmer to take technical ownership of one or two clinical trials from first line of code to final submission package. This is a hands-on statistical programming role with real authority attached to it: you'll be the person a study team turns to when the data needs to hold up under regulatory scrutiny, and the person who decides how a dataset gets built, not just who builds it. You'll work alongside statisticians, data managers, medical writers and regulatory colleagues as a peer, not a downstream resource — reading protocols and SAPs early enough to shape how a study's analysis gets structured, then seeing that structure through to submission-ready SDTM and ADaM datasets, TFLs, and supporting documentation.
Hybrid Based (3 days a week onsite) in Maidenhead
Why It Matters
Clinical data is only as useful as the programming behind it is trustworthy. Every regulatory decision downstream — every safety signal caught or missed, every submission accepted or queried — traces back to whether the datasets and outputs were built right the first time. This role sits at that pressure point. You're not just executing specifications; you're often the one writing them, catching the ambiguity in a protocol before it becomes a data problem three months later, and making the judgment calls that keep a study's analysis both scientifically sound and audit-ready.
What You'll Be Responsible For
You'll lead end-to-end programming for your assigned studies — in-house or outsourced — spanning the full clinical development lifecycle from study setup through analysis, reporting, and regulatory submission. That means building and validating datasets and outputs yourself where the work is done internally, and holding CRO-delivered work to the same bar where it isn't. You'll also be a technical reference point for less experienced programmers, and a contributor to how the wider programming function does its work.
·         Serve as lead programmer for one or two clinical trials, interpreting protocols, SAPs, data management plans, and CRF specifications to drive study setup and analysis
·         Design and validate SDTM and ADaM datasets, tables, figures, and listings, in partnership with study statisticians
·         Review and take ownership of CRO-produced deliverables, ensuring submission-ready quality before they go further
·         Lead specification and delivery of integrated analyses (e.g. ISS/ISE) and associated outputs when not handled by a CRO
·         Mentor other programmers on internal processes and standards, and contribute to departmental tools and process improvements
·         Take on ad hoc analytical work — regulatory query responses, exploratory analyses, publication support — as studies require it
Experience Required
·         Experience of programming in pharmaceutical, biotech, CRO, or clinical research settings
·         Strong SAS proficiency (Base/Macro/Stat/Graph); familiarity with R or other languages is a plus
·         Working knowledge of current CDISC standards — CDASH, SDTM, ADaM, define.xml
·         Track record of producing and validating submission-ready TFLs and datasets, including ad hoc analytical requests
·         Experience supporting regulatory submissions (FDA required; PMDA, NMPA, or EMA experience a plus)
·         Comfort working with external vendors and CRO-managed data
·         BSc in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics or a related field — equivalent experience and certifications will also be considered
About CSL Seqirus
CSL Seqirus is part of CSL. As one of the largest influenza vaccine providers in the world, CSL Seqirus is a major contributor to the prevention of influenza globally and a transcontinental partner in pandemic preparedness. With state-of-the-art production facilities in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia, CSL Seqirus utilizes egg, cell and adjuvant technologies to offer a broad portfolio of differentiated influenza vaccines in more than 20 countries around the world.
To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/.
Our Benefits

You Belong at CSL
At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.
To learn more about inclusion and belonging visit https://www.csl.com/careers/inclusion-and-belonging

Who we are looking for
Our highly successful, multi-faceted eFX trading business is an integral part of State Street Markets offering. Capitalizing on significant growth in revenues, products and capabilities, State Street is investing further into the business to accelerate growth by deploying the latest cutting-edge technology, computational techniques, market insights and talent.
In particular, we seek individuals to enhance our alpha research and trading team, which complements our fully automated market making, benchmark, and client execution algo businesses. This established and successful team of dedicated alpha quants possess a mature research and back testing infrastructure as well access to rich public and proprietary information that can be readily utilized by the right candidate.
We are seeking an individual who can contribute to and extend our existing suite of alpha strategies. Ideal candidates will have a proven track record of developing and deploying systematic trading strategies that generate robust returns net of transaction costs in live trading environments.
We are open to strategies across a range of time horizons, including intraday, event-driven, and longer-horizon approaches. While our core capability today is in spot FX and NDF, we are open to expanding into additional instruments and asset classes in the future (such as FX Swap, cash equities, or futures) where there is a compelling alpha opportunity.
Given the maturity of our infrastructure and platform, we expect candidates to be able to bring research ideas into production within a relatively short time frame, and then build on that foundation to scale and diversify their contribution over time.
Our preferred candidate will have outstanding academics in a hard science, ideally up to PhD level. Substantial practical experience in machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques is also a bonus.
Why this role is important to us
The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Markets (SSM). When owners and managers of institutional assets need research, trading, securities lending and innovative portfolio strategies, they turn to SSM business unit. As our investment research and trading arm, SSM’s number one goal is to enhance and preserve our clients’ portfolio values by applying technology, optimizing trading, and linking asset classes and markets across the world.
Join us if making your mark in the capital markets industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.
What you will be responsible for
As an eFX Alpha Quant Trader you will:
•
Create profitable and robust trading signals, strategies, and models to make a significant contribution to P&L targets and eFX growth
•
Using public and proprietary data, identify new opportunities to generate P&L
•
Develop research all the way from prototype to production
•
Analyze the behaviors of production trading models on an on-going basis, looking for areas of improvement
What we value
These skills will help you succeed in this role:
•
Creative thinkers who are motivated by challenging problems (stochastic, non-stationary, non-linear, partially observed, very low SNR)
•
Ability to complement technical high-frequency analysis with market insights and experience
•
A healthy skepticism about the robustness and generalisability of in-sample results
•
A working habit of first investigating simpler, parsimonious models
•
Desire to work within a collaborative, team-driven environment
Education & Preferred Qualifications
•
Post-graduate degree in a quantitative discipline (engineering, statistics, mathematics, physics, or similar)
•
Experience of a fast prototyping language such as Python (preferably), or Matlab, R, etc..
•
Working knowledge of an industrial scale language such as Java or C++ is a plus
Are you the right candidate? Yes!
We truly believe in the power that comes from the diverse backgrounds and experiences our employees bring with them. Although each vacancy details what we are looking for, we don’t necessarily need you to fulfil all of them when applying. If you like change and innovation, seek to see the bigger picture, make data driven decisions and are a good team player, you could be a great fit.
About State Street
Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.
We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

Job Description:
The Warranty Claims Manager will take end-to-end commercial ownership of supplier warranty issues across Europe, ensuring that defects are resolved efficiently, fairly and in line with Fluence’s contractual warranty rights. Sitting between the technical fix and the formal claim, the role will enforce supplier obligations before issues escalate—determining who is liable for parts and labour, pursuing recovery, and agreeing pragmatic commercial solutions where suppliers struggle to meet their warranty obligations. The role is central to protecting margin, holding suppliers accountable, and positioning Fluence as an organised, priority customer.
Key Responsibilities
•
Review and analyse Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) relating to supplier-provided equipment, and assess the commercial and contractual impact on the affected project.
•
Determine warranty entitlement—confirming whether an issue is covered, and who bears responsibility for parts, labour and associated costs (supplier vs. Fluence).
•
Collaborate with the Quality team on root-cause and 8D analysis to establish the responsible party and capture supporting evidence.
•
Manage and execute the supplier warranty claims process end to end, including notification, documentation, RFIs, follow-up and challenge of supplier rejections.
•
Negotiate and agree commercial solutions where suppliers cannot meet warranty KPIs—for example credit notes, supplier-funded labour, replacement parts, warranty extensions or settlement packages.
•
Act as the single regional point of contact for suppliers on warranty matters, making it straightforward for suppliers to engage and resolve issues quickly.
•
Track and report recovery status, case ageing, credit notes and supplier response times, maintaining accurate records of claims, correspondence and outcomes.
•
Identify patterns and serial defects early, feeding failure data and lessons learned back to Engineering, Quality and Procurement to reduce recurrence.
•
Escalate only material, disputed or strategic matters to the Claims, Legal or Procurement/GPO teams, keeping routine warranty issues out of formal claims.
•
Drive continuous improvement of the warranty process to enhance accountability, recovery rates and supplier performance across the region.
Key Qualifications & Experience
•
Minimum 5+ years’ experience in warranty claims, supplier quality, contract or commercial management, ideally within the construction, energy or industrial manufacturing sectors.
•
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Quality Management, Law, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
•
Strong understanding of supplier warranty agreements and quality-assurance principles, with sound contractual and commercial acumen.
•
Demonstrated experience of NCR processes and root-cause analysis methodologies (e.g. 8D, Six Sigma / Lean).
•
Excellent analytical, communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to hold suppliers to account while maintaining constructive relationships.
•
Able to work independently, manage multiple stakeholders, and coordinate across Quality, Services, Procurement, Project Management, Finance and Legal.
•
Proficient in Microsoft Office and ERP/QMS systems (e.g. SAP, Oracle, or equivalent).
•
Actively contributes to the adoption of AI and digital innovation to support the transformation and future evolution of warranty and claims management (e.g. data analytics, defect-trend detection and process automation).
•
Familiarity with ISO 9001 or similar quality-management systems is desirable.
•
Six Sigma or Lean certification is a plus.
•
English business fluency
